# ASPECT-RASTER cross-implementation reference

How `ASPECT-RASTER` reached E4: compared against GDAL 3.13.1, an implementation
we did not write, on the same frozen analytic DEM the slope reference uses. The
reference and its provenance are committed here; the steps below reproduce it.

## Files

| File | State | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `aspect-gdal.asc` | **committed** | GDAL 3.13.1 Horn aspect, compass degrees, on the DEM's grid. |
| `command.txt` | committed | The exact command that produced `aspect-gdal.asc`. |
| `environment.json` | committed | GDAL/PROJ version, platform, architecture (no generation timestamp is recorded). |
| `SHA256SUMS` | committed | Checksums, including the shared DEM. |

The DEM itself is **not** copied here. It lives at
`../slope/input-dem.asc` and is generated by
`node scripts/make-slope-fixture.mjs`.

## Why the DEM is shared rather than duplicated

One surface, one definition. A second copy could be regenerated or hand-edited
out of step with the first, and then slope and aspect would be validated
against two different surfaces while both READMEs claimed one. `SHA256SUMS`
here pins `../slope/input-dem.asc` by hash, so a DEM that drifts fails the
checksum in this directory as well as in the slope directory.

The surface is `z = a·x² + b·y² + c·x·y + d·x + e·y`, so the gradient — and
therefore the aspect — is exact in closed form. Read
`../slope/README.md` for why the coefficients are what they are, and do not
simplify them: the cross and linear terms are what make a north–south flip
detectable, which matters more for aspect than for slope, because aspect is a
direction.

## Producing the reference

```bash
cd tests/fixtures/reference/aspect
gdaldem aspect ../slope/input-dem.asc aspect-gdal.asc -alg Horn -of AAIGrid
```

Three GDAL defaults are load-bearing here, and each has a flag that would
silently change the meaning of the output:

- **Compass azimuth.** `gdaldem aspect` reports degrees CLOCKWISE FROM NORTH.
  `-trigonometric` switches it to counter-clockwise from east, which is our
  internal frame — it would make the numbers look closer to ours while
  removing the frame conversion the test is there to check. Do not pass it.
- **Flat cells are NODATA.** `-zero_for_flat` would write 0 instead, which is
  a real direction (due north) and would silently turn "no aspect" into "points
  north". Do not pass it. The test excludes near-flat cells by the closed-form
  slope instead, and fails if GDAL wrote NODATA inside that comparison set.
- **Edges excluded.** `gdaldem` drops the one-cell border by default;
  `-compute_edges` opts in. Either is fine — the test drops the border
  regardless, because our kernel clamps at the edge while GDAL leaves it
  undefined, and comparing there would measure a difference in edge policy
  rather than in aspect.

Record in `command.txt` **which binary you ran**, verbatim, not just the flags.

Then:

```bash
gdalinfo --version   # into environment.json, exactly as printed
shasum -a 256 ../slope/input-dem.asc aspect-gdal.asc command.txt environment.json > SHA256SUMS
```

## After the file lands

1. Run `npx vitest run tests/aspectCrossCheck.test.ts`. The skipped case now
   runs and prints the three legs.
2. Only if it passes, flip `ASPECT-RASTER` in `src/validation/crossCheck.ts`
   from `pending` to `supplied`. A test asserts these two move together, so
   flipping the slot without the file — or landing the file without flipping
   the slot — fails.
3. Copy the printed figures into `docs/validation/cross-implementation.md`.
   Read them off the run; do not type them in.

## What this will and will not establish

It compares our Horn aspect against GDAL's Horn aspect: two implementations of
**one** algorithm. That catches coding errors — the v0.4.3 defect recorded in
`src/terrain/ground/terrainDerivatives.ts`, where the ESRI image-row formula
mirrored aspect north–south on our northing-up grid, is exactly the class of
bug this catches — and it is why the closed-form comparison is in the test as
well: two implementations of one method can agree while both being wrong the
same way.

It does not validate the choice of Horn, and it does not touch the point cloud
→ DTM pipeline, since it starts from a DEM. It promotes `ASPECT-RASTER` and
nothing else. `HILLSHADE` consumes aspect but has its own claim and its own
(lower) evidence level, unchanged by this.

## Do not

- **Widen the tolerance.** 0.5° is pre-registered in `REFERENCE_SLOTS` before
  any comparison ran. If the measurement misses it, that is a finding about
  the aspect implementation, not a reason to change the number.
- **Compare bearings by subtraction.** 359° and 1° are 2° apart. The test
  folds every pair to its circular separation first.
- **Compare a defined value against a placeholder.** GDAL's flat NODATA is not
  an aspect of 0.
- **Have the test invoke GDAL.** It compares against the committed artifact, so
  CI needs no GDAL. Shelling out would break CI everywhere it is not installed.
- **Resample to make the grids line up.** The test requires identical
  dimensions. Resampling to force a comparison invents the agreement.
